explain.watched: Created from block {{record}}: the chain watches this vault's Bitcoin from block reports. Its backing is the Bitcoin the chain holds for it, and a key rotation moves the deposit address.
explain.legacy: Created before block {{record}}, so the chain does not watch its Bitcoin. From block {{enforcement}} nothing on it can be spent or withdrawn: holders should move to a watched vault before then.
explain.frozen: Created before block {{record}}, so the chain never watched its Bitcoin. Frozen since block {{enforcement}}: nothing on it can be spent or withdrawn.

withdrawals.heading: Withdrawals
withdrawals.empty: No withdrawals from this vault yet
withdrawals.watchedLifecycle: On a watched vault nobody completes a withdrawal by hand. Once requested, the chain fixes the Bitcoin transaction that pays it from the vault's coins, and the vault's signers broadcast it; the requester can raise its fee or give it up (a release). It is paid when a Bitcoin report sees that transaction confirmed, and closed with the vBTC returned (less the release's Bitcoin fee, for a release) if it is released, cancelled before it is fixed, or expires. A Bitcoin reorg can reopen a paid withdrawal until it is paid again.
